title: The Other Side of Bug Localization - Semiwiki
gist: Bernard Murphy argues that agentic chip-debug tooling has solved the RTL side but not the software side of bug localization, because gdb-style on-the-fly debuggers give agents no recorded runtime history to reason backwards from. He positions Undo's record-and-replay debugger — exposed to agents via an MCP server, demonstrated jointly with Anthropic at C++ Con — as the missing substrate, and proposes a divide-and-conquer flow pairing agentic RTL debug with agentic software debug at the hardware/software interface. The piece closes as a DAC 2026 booth promo for Undo.

insights.claim: Debug remains the most time- and resource-consuming part of verification, which is itself the most time- and resource-consuming part of modern chip/system design, making automated root-cause localization the highest-leverage target for agentic EDA automation.
insights.speaker: Bernard Murphy
insights.so_what: Verification-debug is where EDA vendors can monetize AI fastest — watch which EDA and debug-tool suppliers attach agents to the debug loop rather than to RTL generation.
insights.quote: debug remains the most time and resource-consuming aspect of verification, in turn the most time/resource-consuming aspect of modern chip/system design

insights.claim: Bug root causes in chip projects are as likely to sit in the software test infrastructure around the RTL — virtual/HLS models, reference models, firmware and the test stack — as in the RTL itself, so RTL-only debug automation addresses at best half the problem.
insights.speaker: Bernard Murphy
insights.so_what: A debug-automation vendor whose coverage stops at RTL is structurally capped; tool spend should shift toward suppliers that span the software test stack.
insights.quote: it is already clear that root-causes are just as likely to be found in the software test infrastructure around the RTL
insights.locator: Key takeaways — For many of us, attention is naturally biased

insights.claim: Agentic debug works in RTL simulation because simulators already save detailed state history for later traceback, whereas conventional software debug depends on human-driven on-the-fly stepping with no recording — the asymmetry, not model quality, is why software-side agentic debug lags.
insights.speaker: Bernard Murphy
insights.so_what: The binding constraint on AI debug is recorded runtime state, so infrastructure that captures execution history is the choke point worth owning, not the LLM layer.
insights.quote: Not a problem in RTL simulation systems which save detailed state history for later traceback, but such recording is uncommon in software debug
insights.locator: Agentic debugging on the test stack

insights.claim: The atomic command set of common software debuggers such as gdb is a poor reasoning interface for AI agents, which struggle to decide next steps from it even though gdb has served human debuggers well for decades.
insights.speaker: Bernard Murphy
insights.so_what: Incumbent open-source debug tooling does not automatically extend into the agentic era — an opening for commercial replay-based debuggers to take share.
insights.quote: It is difficult for an agent to reason to next steps using the atomic commands available in common software debuggers.
insights.locator: Agentic debugging on the test stack

insights.claim: Agentic debug must reason backwards from an observed misbehavior rather than forwards as humans typically do, which inverts the workflow that existing software debuggers were designed around.
insights.speaker: Bernard Murphy
insights.so_what: Backward traceback is a design requirement, not a feature — evaluate debug-tool vendors on reverse execution capability rather than on AI branding.
insights.quote: the goal is to trace back from a misbehavior rather than forward (as is common in human debug)
insights.locator: Agentic debugging on the test stack

insights.claim: The hope that agents could localize bugs from static code analysis alone has been empirically disproven; historical dynamic runtime context is required in addition to static learning.
insights.speaker: Bernard Murphy
insights.so_what: Discounts pure code-reading AI debug startups and favors those instrumenting execution — a filter for private AI-devtools deals.
insights.quote: The hope had been that agents could learn enough behavior from a static analysis of the code to support such reasoning, but experience has shown that hope was too optimistic.
insights.locator: Agentic debugging on the test stack

themes.theme: Undo's record-and-replay as the agentic substrate

insights.claim: Undo's debugger traces back through a runtime recording, which users say makes it distinctively effective at non-deterministic failures such as thread races that conventional debuggers cannot reliably reproduce.
insights.speaker: Bernard Murphy
insights.so_what: Non-determinism is the highest-pain, lowest-substitutability debug segment — pricing power sits with whoever solves it.
insights.quote: Users comment that Undo is particularly useful when trying to track down non-deterministic behavior (thread races for example).
insights.locator: Undo is optimized for agentic software debug

insights.claim: Undo is already entrenched beyond its known networking-software base into EDA, HLS and virtual modeling teams, meaning chip companies' software organizations may already be paying for the substrate their verification agents will need.
insights.speaker: Bernard Murphy
insights.so_what: An existing installed base lowers the adoption barrier for agentic debug in semis — a land-and-expand setup rather than a greenfield sale.
insights.locator: Undo is optimized for agentic software debug

insights.claim: Undo exposes its recording and technology to AI agents through an MCP server, letting an agent combine runtime context with static code learning to progressively trace an observed issue back to candidate root causes.
insights.speaker: Bernard Murphy
insights.so_what: MCP is becoming the default integration layer for developer-tool AI — watch it as the de facto standard determining which tools get agent distribution.
insights.quote: Undo provides access to their tech and a recording through an MCP server.
insights.locator: Undo is optimized for agentic software debug

insights.claim: In a live joint Undo-Anthropic exercise at C++ Con, agents tracked down a crash in the Python interpreter and surfaced a non-obvious non-bug behavior, with human-in-the-loop discovery that was significantly more efficient than conventional debug.
insights.speaker: Bernard Murphy
insights.so_what: Evidence that agentic debug is at demo-to-early-deployment stage, not production-autonomous — efficiency gains are real but still supervised.
insights.quote: Examples shown were human-in-the-loop discovery, as you might expect, but significantly more efficient than conventional debug.
insights.locator: Undo is optimized for agentic software debug

insights.claim: A single agentic flow spanning hardware and software debug is not achievable today, so the practical architecture is divide-and-conquer: agentic software debug against a virtual reference model early, and mirrored software-side traceback when RTL debug reaches the hardware/software interface later.
insights.speaker: Bernard Murphy
insights.so_what: Near-term EDA AI value accrues to point tools that stitch together, not to a unified platform — a caution against paying platform multiples too early.
insights.quote: It would be nice to imagine a solution that could span both hardware and software in one flow, but I’m not sure that is possible today.
insights.locator: How could this work with RTL debug?
